traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Juglandaceae with Rhoipteleaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves usually alternate, rarely opposite; leaves compound; compound leaves pinnate; veins pinnate; leaves deciduous; stipules usually absent, sometimes present; plants usually monoecious, sometimes hermaphrodite or polygamous, rarely dioecious; ovary usually inferior, sometimes superior; stems usually woody, sometimes herbaceous; flowers usually in catkins, sometimes solitary, in racemes or in spikes; perianth tepals or absent; fruit nut or samara, sometimes drupe; stamens (3-) 5 to 50 (-100); carpels 2 (-3). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 339, 340, 341, family Juglandaceae: leaf margin serrate, often; read as {"serrate": "often"}.

traits.stamens.note: Rare extremes noted only; the count's source is the family's `traits` note. The books give the family low 2: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 339, 340, 341: 2-∞. Left out of the range on the owner's go (2026-10-15): they belong to some of its genera, and a family's rare ends would reach every species that inherits its count.
